summary.oneLiner: Uni Abex Alloy Products Limited, established in 1972 and part of the family-owned Neterwala Group, is recognised as a leading manufacturer of centrifugal castings in India, supplying high-durability heat-, wear- and corrosion-resistant alloy components for critical industrial applications.
summary.business: Uni Abex specialises in the manufacture of premium alloy steel castings, particularly for decanters and reformer tubes, with a product portfolio spanning radiant tubes, retort tubes, air injection tubes, tube support castings, tube sheets and header assemblies. It supplies high-durability components for demanding applications across industries including fertilisers, refining, direct reduction of iron, hydrogen and ammonia, combining centrifugal casting with static castings for high-performance, critical-use environments. The Company positions itself on a quality-first approach, timely delivery, productivity improvement and industry-approved welding procedures, supported by in-house R&D and academic collaborations.

Materials / alloys: R-Alloy (new material commercialised in FY 2025-26 with successful customer deliveries)

currentContext.expansion: The Board has approved a capital outlay of Rs.121 crore towards strengthening the Company's production and operational capabilities, described in the Chairman/CFO commentary as planned capital expenditure for FY 2026-27 focused on the Bay-3 expansion. Management frames this as capacity enhancement through plant expansion to support increasing demand from global markets and specialised applications, and points to significant value-creation opportunities from the Bay-3 expansion, automation initiatives, a new manufacturing facility and continued investments in specialised petrochemical and catalyst tube applications. Alongside the physical expansion, the Company is developing an end-to-end automated reformer production line, expanding low-cost automation and strengthening digital manufacturing capabilities to support future capacity expansion, with continued investment in automation, TPM, IoT-enabled Spectro analysis, digital quality systems and advanced welding technologies. A SAP implementation is under way to integrate operational and financial systems. On the operating side FY 2025-26 saw total pouring volume rise 11% to 4,172 MT with the highest melting output achieved in two consecutive months, pull-boring productivity improved from 8 to over 10 tubes per day, and 150 assemblies fabricated with 170 dispatched in March 2026. No commissioning date, completion date or capacity addition figure is disclosed for Bay-3 or for the new manufacturing facility, and R&D capital expenditure for the year is stated as Rs. Nil.

risks.note: Management names volatility in raw material prices as one of the two key risks identified. Uni Abex's alloy castings are nickel- and other-alloy intensive, so input cost swings hit margins directly. Mitigation disclosed: sourcing from multiple suppliers to ensure supply continuity and cost-effective procurement, active monitoring of raw material markets, strategic inventory positions, strategic stockpiling of critical materials and long-term arrangements with major suppliers.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure on imports and exports
risks.note: Foreign exchange rate movements may affect the Company's international business, including material imports and goods exports - a structural exposure given the deliberate push into MENA, North America and Asia-Pacific export markets. Mitigation disclosed: hedging measures through contractual arrangements, with forex exposures continuously reviewed.

risks.risk: Macroeconomic and geopolitical shocks, including the Middle East conflict and tariffs
risks.note: Management flags that unexpected shifts in the economic environment can impact operations and profitability, that the war in the Middle East threatens to disrupt growth and disinflation, and that material changes such as tariffs, the current war situation and linked commodity processes may put uncertainty in the business environment which may affect the financial position. The exposure is doubled-sided because MENA is both a target growth region and the source of the geopolitical disruption; energy commodity prices are projected to rise 19% in 2026 with oil up 21.4%.

risks.risk: Tightening environmental regulation and carbon border compliance
risks.note: Increasing environmental concerns and the tightening of related regulations are placing additional pressure on manufacturers, especially in managing emissions and waste, and compliance with these evolving norms could lead to higher operational costs which may affect overall industry performance. For an exporter this extends to carbon border regimes - the Company reports having achieved CBAM compliance during the year.

risks.risk: Skilled technical manpower shortage, particularly welders
risks.note: The Company reports having had to address skilled welder shortages by recruiting from technical institutes and providing 2-3 week structured on-the-job training to build an internal talent pool. With a total permanent workforce of only 103 employees as at 31 March 2026, availability of specialised welding and metallurgical skills is a genuine constraint on scaling output and on executing the planned Bay-3 expansion.

The Company experienced LPG supply disruptions during the year and mitigated them by establishing three independent private supply sources to guarantee zero production downtime. Melting and heat-treatment operations are energy-intensive, so continuity of fuel and power supply is a direct production risk.

risks.risk: Customer, geographic and end-use concentration with project-order cyclicality
risks.note: Management explicitly cites diversification across customers, geographies and end-use industries as the means of reducing concentration risk and market cyclicality - an acknowledgement that the exposure exists. Revenue is driven by a relatively small number of large project orders (execution of large orders from NFL, NRL and CPCL named as a driver of the year's performance, against a record order book of approximately Rs.77 crore), and demand is concentrated in petrochemical, fertiliser and refinery reformer applications, making revenue lumpy and tied to those sectors' capex cycles.

risks.risk: Broad business and economic risks identified by the Board
risks.note: The Board's risk management policy states the Company, like all business in the country, is exposed to business and economic risks arising out of war, market conditions, vagaries of monsoon, tariffs and commodity risks. The Board has identified risks and steps to mitigate them, with the executive management operating an adequately defined risk-management framework.
